title: Instant Access Savings: 5.50% p.a. Variable for 3 Months on up to $100,000, Interest Paid Daily (New Customers) @ Revolut
body:
Deal: Instant Access Savings: 5.50% p.a. Variable for 3 Months on up to $100,000, Interest Paid Daily (New Customers) @ Revolut

[payton] yep, allows up to $500K balance and just needs a single $100 top up each month 6% intro rate for 4 months, too.
Offer is dead in the water.
[tunzafun001] I had an account with ING I closed 22 years ago. .. made me ineligible for their bonus saver…..
[payton] Quite harsh for the bank to not grant someone the welcome rate - a mere 0.6% increase over the regular, because of an account closed that long ago :|
[tunzafun001] @payton: Was a first for me…. So i went elsewhere.
Also asked for a please explain why they were still retaining my information 20+ years later (I specifically request it is deleted). AFCA intervened..
[payton] Any chance you can change your referral system so the signup bonus is split even between the referrer and referee?
This is the common setup for companies offering a referral system.
[VladImpaler] Some of us are happy to accept the full amount 😉
[payton] The referee had to do the legwork, 3x $10 transactions, pays $10 for card delivery but gets paid zilch. The invite is not its own reward xD
Ozb's guidelines states that referrals should benefit both parties.
Can I post a deal that is about a store’s referral system?
You may post a deal that is for the retailer's referral system, under the basis the referee also earns credit and it has not been posted previously (unless it is a temporary offer that had previously expired) or is already included in the OzBargain referral system.
@RevolutOz
Please also stop randomising how many days a referee is given to complete the 3x $10 spends.
All other banks have a simple 'spend X in 30 days' instead of randomising how many days are alloted. It gives the bank an easy loophole to deny payment but a PITA for everyone else.
[mmrazz] Ongoing rates (and above $100k) - https://www.revolut.com/en-AU/legal/interest-rates-and-fees/
Basically, medocre unless you're willing to pay $100/month to get "Ultra".
[runamuck] Rubbish deal. Why even bother? If you want to play the intro game of 3 - 4 months, you are not even close.
Rabo HISA - 5.90%
Ubank Saver - 5.85%
Bankwest Easy saver - 5.75%
[tunzafun001] I think rabo is now 6%. Saw it somewhere today.
[wl au] Be very careful with Revolut.
A friend prepaid $999 for their Ultra Plan and applied for a credit card. He incorrectly entered $1000 for his credit limit instead of $10,000.
After many calls and hours on the phone to Revolut, they have refused to increase his credit limit to $10,000. He was informed he had to cancel his credit card and then re-apply for a new credit card with a $10,000 limit.
So he cancelled the credit card, but they have now rejected his new credit card application and have refused to refund the $999 annual fee. He was so disgusted by their blatant lies that he has vowed to NEVER deal with them again. I have suggested that he lodge a complaint with the Banking Ombudsman.
Absolutely terrible support staff that bounce you around and they have no idea on how to increase a credit card limit. Revolut is just out to charge you as much as they can. Read all their terms and conditions very carefully before you give them any money.
[askbargain] I think credit limit increase thing is global for Revolut which is odd to see it here. Not sure if it’s common elsewhere.
[wl au] HI askbargain, do you mean it is a global issue?
[askbargain] I also have a 1k limit and was curious to see why there’s a decrease button but not increase.
You can see people in Europe having the same issue.
https://www.reddit.com/r/Revolut/comments/1kh6bnc/credit_car…
I don’t need a higher limit so I don’t bother.
[wl au] Wow, thank you so much for the link askbargain. Much appreciated.
I had recommended that he sign up to Revolut because they give you 1 Avios point for $1 spent. Now I feel really bad because they have ripped him of $999, but refused to give him a new credit card.
Now, I really wish I had never heard of this horrible company.
